question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{tanh}^{2}⁡x}{2{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

$$

First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{tanh}^{2}⁡x}{2{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {tanh}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now we need to find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Then, we use the above identity to write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {tanh}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{sech}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+1}-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{4}{5}-\frac{3}{5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$
